Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:95956

Case :- Application U/S 528 Bnss No. - 16657 of 2025
Applicant :- Ratnakar Singh

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Prakash Chandra Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Jitendra Kumar Sinha,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Aga for the State and perused the record.

2. The present application has been filed with the prayer to quash the charge sheet and proceeding
in pursuance to charge sheet no. 01, dated 04.12.2023, i.e. case no. 6568 of 2024 (State Vs. Ratnakar
Singh), under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468 & 471 Ipc relating to case crime no. 554 of 2023, P.S. Line
Bazar, District Jaunpur, pending in the court of Cjm, Jaunpur and further prayed to stay the
aforesaid proceeding.

3.  Learned counsel for the applicant submits that as per the allegation in the F.I.R., the applicant has been attributed with the allegation of submitting forged FDRs for obtaining government tender while he was working as a government contractor in the year 2019-2020.
Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that the same allegation has been leveled after four years in the year 2023 and there is no explanation for the delay.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that the Investigating Officer has not obtained the original FDRs rather the Investigating Officer has conducted investigation on the basis of photocopy of FDRs.

It is further submitted that no offence is Ratnakar Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73467403/
1 made out and the charge sheet filed is an abuse of the process of Court.
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned AGA submits that the Investigating Officer has got verified the FDRs from the bank concerned and has found the said FDRs to be forged and has conducted the investigation in a fair and impartial manner and submitted the charge sheet in accordance with law.
Learned AGA further submits that the present application lacks merit and is fit to be dismissed.

5. The law regarding quashing of the charge sheet has been dealt by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Bihar Vs. Radendra Agarwal JT 1996 (1) 601, 1996 SCALE (1) 394 in which the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that at the stage of taking cognizance the Court is not required to sift the evidence, the Court is only required to see whether any offence is made out or not.

entities.text: State of Bihar Vs. Radendra Agarwal JT 1996 (1) 601, 1996 SCALE (1) 394
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. As per the F.I.R., the applicant has been attributed with the allegation of submitting forged FDRs and the Investigating Officer has submitted the charge sheet after completing the investigation, at this stage it cannot be said that no offence is made out.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that though the charge sheet has been submitted u/s 419, 420, 467, 468 & 471 of IPC but the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance u/s 210 (1) BNSS, 2023.
Learned counsel for the applicant points out that the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance under Section 210 (1) BNSS which reflects that the learned Magistrate has not applied his mind.
8. At this stage, learned AGA submits that the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance of the offence u/s 419, 420, 467, 468 & 471 of IPC under the provision of Section 210 (1) BNSS.

9. On perusal of the order impugned it appears that the learned Magistrate has mentioned the provisions of Section 210 (1) BNSS which is a procedural law and which empowers the Magistrate to take cognizance.
10. By quoting the provision of BNSS which empowers the Magistrate to take cognizance is not the material irregularity or illegality which can vitiate the order of cognizance.

The learned Magistrate has referred that the charge sheet against the applicant has been filed u/s 419, 420, 467, 468 & 471 of IPC, hence, in view of the above, the present application lacks merit and deserves to be dismissed.
11. Application is accordingly, dismissed.
